controls.finding: Consumed successful v4; not VM evidence.
Configuration ID, root and --uuid bind exact runtime service; no VM instance created.
Reviewed bytes, kernel/init/rootfs references, published artifact pins and file identity; no atomic check/use guarantee.
Checks later config/kernel/rootfs metadata and copied content against sealed create output. No actual bundle created; sparse-shape mismatch refuses.
One seal, exact role source/argv/PID/UID/birth/executable, runtime plist/source, original boot/deadline. No live observer/runner is supplied.
Object holder can query state or receive delegate notifications; no documented hard observation/stop latency.
No supported external live-instance lookup/adoption/backend identity in audited public interface; runtime status and PID disappearance insufficient.
Helper names/relationships are implementation details; no direct mapping technique. Shared helpers cannot safely be classified or killed by name.
Successful callback denotes stop for the held object; errors/state transitions must be checked; no guaranteed completion deadline.
OS is expected to clean up the client VM. Does not independently establish this host deadline, backend identities or quiescence.
Hostname->Attachment lookup and session-bound allocation release are supported. Lookup absence is not VM/interface teardown proof.
Requires interface_ref; immediate success schedules callback. Serializable network_ref is a network capability, not interface/VM adoption.
Empty attachments mean empty interface/session construction loop; not a host-observed network/IPC denial or cleanup proof.
No supported observer combines exact VM execution/backend and interface/session quiescence after runtime death. Primary terminal blocker.
Never rearm; reject changed identities/provenance; no bootstrap/actions or successful teardown; preserve state and refuse retry.
Proposed read-only shares do not establish observed enforcement.
No guest/VM run; workload rlimits/cgroups are not a whole-host aggregate proof.
Unsupported independent ownership/teardown contract blocks first bounded VM experiment.

next_decision: Keep Apple stack disabled pending supported external instance control/observation, or separately authorize evaluation of a different ownership boundary. No implementation/redesign/live effects authorized.
